sources.locator: Complete §§3.1–3.2, printed pp. 16–29 (PDF pp. 19–32); all numbered headings Definition 3.2 through Lemma 3.14, plus section headings and unnumbered classification/calculus paragraphs. Reconciliation inspection expanded the original pp.16–26 locator to include the rest of §3.2.
sources.disposition: used; complete proof route inspected, with local hypotheses and the orthogonality component stated explicitly

contents.name: 3.1 Generalized inverses
contents.reason: The local definition and well-definedness proof supply the exact-data minimum-norm construction; the additional least-squares results below are separately deferred.

contents.name: Definition 3.2: least squares solution and minimum norm solution
contents.reason: The local Moore–Penrose definition proves minimum norm for an exact solvable range component. The general least-squares minimization definition, including unattained minima, is additional Hilbert-space scope requiring owner placement.

contents.name: Theorem 3.3: Hilbert-space Moore–Penrose inverse, domain and nullspace
Lemma 3.4: range and four Moore–Penrose equations
contents.reason: The local definition verifies its inverse construction, but does not state or prove all four projection identities as a separate result; that full Hilbert-space package needs an owner placement decision.

contents.name: Theorem 3.5: least-squares solutions and unique minimum norm solution
contents.reason: The exact-preimage minimum-norm portion is proved locally, while the complete least-squares existence/affine-kernel classification for arbitrary domain data is not claimed by this six-item pair and needs explicit owner placement.

contents.name: Corollary 3.6: least squares and normal equations
contents.reason: The arbitrary Hilbert-space normal-equation characterization is beyond the approved compact range/Picard inventory; the published finite-matrix normal-equation results do not discharge that infinite-dimensional claim.

contents.name: Theorem 3.7: continuity of the pseudoinverse iff closed range
contents.scope_note: The source treats every bounded Hilbert operator; the authored theorem states and proves the compact-operator specialization only.

contents.name: Corollary 3.8: compact infinite-dimensional range implies discontinuous pseudoinverse
3.2 Singular value decomposition of compact operators
Theorem 3.9: compact singular system and expansion
Theorem 3.10: Picard criterion and pseudoinverse series
Moderately, severely and exponentially ill-posed problems (unnumbered classification)
contents.reason: This source paragraph classifies singular-value decay and perturbation amplification. Quantitative spectral ill-posedness/source assumptions belong to the planned deterministic-rate development, rather than the basic range criterion.

contents.name: Example 3.11: Volterra integration singular system and differentiation
contents.reason: This continuous integral-operator computation requires differential/integral and boundary-condition arguments not used by the approved diagonal sequence witness; retain it for the numerical-differentiation development.

contents.name: Functional calculus phi(K* K), equations (3.16)–(3.17)
contents.reason: The operator functional calculus is introduced after the Picard example and supports later spectral filters; it is not asserted by the compact inverse-map definition or its range criterion.

contents.name: Example 3.12: identity, K* K and absolute value |K| via functional calculus
contents.reason: These examples define the compact-operator absolute value and calculus needed for filters and source powers; they belong with the spectral regularization framework.

contents.name: Lemma 3.13: powers, selfadjointness, norm and range properties of |K|
contents.reason: The power and range identities are prerequisites for source-space analysis, not premises of the local Picard proof, and should be developed with deterministic source conditions.

contents.name: Lemma 3.14: interpolation inequality for operator powers
contents.reason: This Holder interpolation estimate establishes source-power rate bounds and is unused by the exact range/Picard arguments; the planned source-condition page is its natural destination.
